minutes.headline: Commission voted to tell Selectmen it wants a donated landlocked parcel; solar hearing continued two weeks.
minutes.summary: The commission voted to express interest to the Selectmen in acquiring a donated landlocked parcel, heard an Eagle Scout trail-access project, and issued determinations on several requests. The solar field hearing was continued two weeks for a construction sequencing schedule, with the applicant offering a conservation restriction on remaining land. Enforcement updates covered a possible stop work order and a lien versus lawsuit question.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission voted unanimously to tell the Board of Selectmen it is interested in acquiring a donated landlocked parcel.
The solar field notice of intent hearing was continued to November 1 so the applicant can supply a construction sequencing schedule; the vote was not audible.
Negative determinations were issued for 455 Townsend Harbor Road (with a permeable paver condition), a carport at 52 Pearl Street, and 425 West Townsend Road.
A Scout presented an Eagle project to move a gate, enlarge parking and add benches; the commission set a Saturday site visit.
The town manager must still find a funding source for back taxes on the donated parcel, which is also being checked against a land value threshold.

why_it_matters: Accepting donated land can put back taxes and upkeep on the town budget, mostly taxes, and the parcel may come to residents as a warrant article at Town Meeting.
The solar field decision affects how nearby conservation land is protected and built around, including any conservation restriction on the remaining land.
watch_next: The continued solar field hearing on November 1, with the construction sequencing schedule due.
Warrant articles the town manager is preparing on the donated parcel, and the Selectmen's response.
